title: Leftover prompt and parent wake name a PR the build only read, not the one it opened
description:
## As asked

**Problem.** When a build reads other PRs while it works, the PR named in its `leftover` prompt, and in the parent's wake, can be one it only read instead of the one it opened.

Two pieces pick the PR, and both prefer how often a link was mentioned over the session's own report:

* **simple-dispatcher** `hook.js buildEvidence` (about line 589): the terminal `[done]` entry's `url` is `canonical = report.tracked[0]`, the tracked link mentioned most often in the transcript.
* **Harbour** `lib/dispatch-wake.js prUrlOfFeedback` (line 279): for the newest entry it checks `url` before `message`. So the session's own `DONE:` line (in `message`) loses to the `url` from the first point.

**Witness.** In LIN-4374's build, PR #2357 was mentioned 11 times because the build read the parent's comments. The build opened and reported PR #2359 on its `DONE:` line, but its leftover prompt named #2357 (see LIN-4374's `### Leftovers` comment, `60c78ab6`). Review confirmed both code paths (LIN-4374 review comment `f69f770f`).

**Why it matters.** The leftover step asks a builder to tidy "its" PR, and the parent's wake tells the next step which PR to act on. When the PR is wrong, the tidy can land on the wrong branch, or the next stage reads an unrelated PR. This is likely for any build that reads earlier pieces of an epic, which is the normal case for multi-piece work.

**Acceptance.**

* When a session reports a PR on its `DONE:` line, or opened a PR in its own transcript, that PR is the `[done]` entry's `url` in `hook.js`, whatever the mention counts are.
* `prUrlOfFeedback` returns the PR the session reported on its `[done]` / `DONE:` message ahead of an `url` field that disagrees with it.
* Each repo has a test with a transcript or feedback that mentions another PR more often than the session's own. The test asserts the session's own PR wins.

**File anchors.** `simple-dispatcher/hook.js` (`buildEvidence`, `buildLinkReport`); `LinearViewer/lib/dispatch-wake.js:279` (`prUrlOfFeedback`) and its callers `withHeldWakeNote` and the leftover prompt's `prUrl`.

**Priority reasoning.** High (`priorityLevel` 3): the prompt names the wrong PR, which can misdirect a push or a stage. It recurs on any build that reads sibling PRs, but it does not lose data.

Filed from LIN-4374's close-out as an outside follow-up (parent effort LIN-4347).

### Unvalidated idea

In `buildEvidence`, rank a PR that appears in the session's final `DONE:` line, or a PR the session created (`gh pr create` output), above frequency. In `prUrlOfFeedback`, when the newest entry's `message` carries a PR URL, prefer it over `url`.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Implemented

Done. Merged and deployed on 2026-11-08:

* Harbour [#2360](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2360>) (`459f8711`): `prUrlOfFeedback` reads the PR from the newest `DONE:`/`[done]` line ahead of a disagreeing `url`. It also adds the `claimLeftoverFor` claim, released on every skip after the claim; review accepted this addition for LIN-4347.
* simple-dispatcher [#330](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/330>) (`cb79e00`): the `[done]` url is the session's own PR, from its `DONE:` line or `gh pr create`, ahead of mention counts.

Built as asked, plus the accepted claim addition. On the landed code, the LIN-4374 witness now resolves to #2359 in both repos. The live end-to-end check is recorded as not run in the close-out comment. The full history is kept in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

comments.body:
**Built, as part of LIN-4347's revision (both repos).** PRs:

- https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/330, head `ffe2ad85`, CI green.
- https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2360, head `e0dc01f3`, CI green.

The acceptance, point by point:

- **The `[done]` url in `hook.js`.** A PR on the session's `DONE:` line wins, then a PR its `gh pr create` printed, whatever the mention counts. This lives in `selectCanonical` and `sessionPrs` (`links.js`). Only tracked, in-scope PRs can win, so the scope rule still applies.
- **`prUrlOfFeedback`.** It now returns the PR on a `DONE:` or `[done]` line ahead of a disagreeing `url` field.
- **One test per repo** where another PR is mentioned more often (the LIN-4374 shape, #2357 ×26 vs #2359 on `DONE:`). Both failed on unfixed code with `actual …/2357, expected …/2359`, and both pass now:
  - `test/lin-4375-session-pr.test.js`
  - `tests/unit/lin-4375-session-pr-wins.test.js`

The Harbour PR also fixes the duplicate-enqueue race from the LIN-4347 review: `claimLeftoverFor` is a compare-and-set claim, and a concurrent-`[done]` test expects exactly one leftover row.

Next: review, merge and deploy both PRs. Merging is not mine.

## Review — LIN-4375

I reviewed Harbour [PR #2360](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2360) at head `a874f03f` and simple-dispatcher [PR #330](https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/330) at head `2bb9dc80`. Both are open, mergeable and based on current `main` (LinearViewer `d5d18e6d`, simple-dispatcher `07c88f7`).

CI: green on both heads. #2360: Unit tests, E2E 1–4/4, Secret scan, CI success. #330: unit tests. I also re-ran the full simple-dispatcher suite on `2bb9dc80`: 4268 pass, 0 fail.

### What I checked myself
- **Scope.** The PR-selection fix matches the ticket's file anchors: `hook.js buildEvidence` with `links.js` `sessionPrs`/`selectCanonical`, and `prUrlOfFeedback` in `lib/dispatch-wake.js`. Every caller of `prUrlOfFeedback` inherits the fix: `lineagePrUrl` (leftover prompt), and `dispatch-store.js:3415/3422/3521` (held-wake notes). **Overrun:** #2360 also adds the `claimLeftoverFor` compare-and-set, which this ticket did not ask for. It answers LIN-4347's review (`0ef19446`). The builder disclosed it, and LIN-4347's re-review accepted it. I reviewed it as part of this PR, and it has the defect below.
- **Staleness.** Since this ticket was filed, the only commit touching the anchored files is `d5d18e6d` (LIN-4374), which this PR is based on. The ticket's description still holds.
- **Regression check.** `git log -8` on `hook.js`, `links.js`, `dispatch-wake.js`, `dispatch-leftover-hook.js` and `dispatch-store.js` shows no earlier fix to PR selection or the claim path that this undoes, and no reverts.
- **Mutation checks** (each one reverted; both worktrees are clean):
  - Harbour: removed the reported-PR loop in `prUrlOfFeedback` → 4 of 10 fail, including LIN-4374's shape and the store-level prompt/wake test. Skipped the `claimLeftoverFor` check in the hook → 1 fails ("exactly one leftover row").
  - simple-dispatcher: `selectCanonical` ignores the session's own PRs → 3 of 7 fail. Removed `gh pr create` harvesting → 2 fail. `buildEvidence` unwired back to `tracked[0]` → 3 fail, which shows the hook really calls the new code.
- **Test level** is right. The Harbour tests go through `addFeedback` with the real leftover hook, and the simple-dispatcher tests go through `buildEvidence` on a transcript file.

### Finding (defect, Request Changes): a claim winner that skips can strand the parent wake on a re-report
`claimLeftoverFor` stamps `leftoverClaimedAt` and never clears it. The hook header and doc comment reason that a winner that skips "wakes the parent itself, so a later re-report reads `parent-already-woken`". That holds only when the wake is actually minted. `_deliverWake` **withdraws** the wake on a transient failure, without burning the witness, and relies on the runner's LIN-3805 re-report to retry. The failures are: the declaration lookup fault, `getItemStatus` fault, and a provisioner `reason` such as `grant-mint-transient:*` (`dispatch-store.js` ~3790–3855). On that re-report, `decideLeftover` answers `queue` again: there is no leftover row and the parent has not been woken. Then `claimLeftoverFor` loses to the first post's stale stamp, and the hook answers `hold` with no row to release it. **The parent is never woken.**

Repro (a scratch test, since deleted): two consecutive `[done]` posts, no concurrency. The first has an enqueue that returns 503 `OWNER_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE` and a provisioner that returns `{reason:'grant-mint-transient:x'}`. The second has a healthy provisioner.
- `main` `d5d18e6d`: passes. The logs show two `skipped reason=enqueue-503` lines, then `[dispatch-wake] enqueued parent=…`: one wake.
- PR head `a874f03f`: **fails** (`actual: 0, expected: 1` wakes). The logs show `skipped reason=enqueue-503`, then `[leftover] hold item=… claim-lost`.

The two transient faults are correlated: an owner-check outage refuses the enqueue and also fails the declared-grant mint. So this is not the "server dies between two awaits" residual that LIN-4347's re-review accepted. It is a new stall path that `main` does not have.

**The fix (implementation):** in `lib/dispatch-leftover-hook.js`, once `claimLeftoverFor` has returned true, every later `skip` path should release the claim before it returns. Those paths are `no-base-url`, `no-workspace` and `enqueue-<status>`. Add `DispatchQueueStore.releaseLeftoverClaim(urlKey, itemId)`: `updateOne({_id, urlKey}, {$unset: {leftoverClaimedAt: ''}})`, best-effort and logged. A concurrent loser has already answered `hold`, and the winner's skip still delivers the one wake, so the concurrent test keeps passing. Add the repro above to `tests/unit/lin-4375-session-pr-wins.test.js`: after the transient withdrawal, the re-report wakes the parent once, or queues one leftover row. Then update the hook header, `dispatch-and-proxy.md` "One claim per row" and the `runs-and-dispatch` lesson to match.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is "which PR is this session's". Its places are the runner's `[done]` url (`selectCanonical`) and Harbour's `prUrlOfFeedback`, and both are handled. `lib/run-evidence.js` and `lib/ci-wake-sweep.js` collect every PR on purpose, which is a different mechanism. One **inside** sibling is still open, as LIN-4347's re-review found and I confirmed. `links.js sessionPrs` reverses the flattened URL list. So `DONE: opened …/LinearViewer/pull/2360 and …/simple-dispatcher/pull/330` gives `reported[0] === …/simple-dispatcher/pull/330` (the last PR), while Harbour's `reportedPrUrlOf` takes the first.

### Leftovers at the edges
I checked the `### Leftovers` comment on LIN-4347 (`ecf378ee`) against the diff. The doc tidy and the three Waiting entries are present and worded correctly. I found no other untouched edge. The claim defect above is a defect, not a leftover.

### Against the As-asked block
- "When a session reports a PR on its `DONE:` line, or opened a PR in its own transcript, that PR is the `[done]` entry's `url`…": **met** (`selectCanonical`; tests 1–3, mutation-checked). With two PRs on one line, the last one wins (see the sibling above).
- "`prUrlOfFeedback` returns the PR the session reported on its `[done]` / `DONE:` message ahead of an `url` field that disagrees": **met** (`reportedPrUrlOf`, tests, M1).
- "Each repo has a test with a transcript or feedback that mentions another PR more often than the session's own…": **met** in both repos (#2357 ×26 vs #2359).
- The rest (problem, witness, why, anchors, priority) is context, and the work addresses it at its cause.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **inside** (the claim this PR adds; the transient-withdrawal re-report). CI has no test where a claim winner skips and its wake is then withdrawn. *Before the merge:* the fix above, plus the repro test. Deciding condition: a re-reported `[done]` after `enqueue-503` together with `grant-mint-transient` produces exactly one parent wake, not `claim-lost`.
- **inside** (the PR selection class; two PRs on one `DONE:` line). *Before the merge:* in `links.js sessionPrs`, push each `DONE:` line's PRs as one group and reverse the **groups**, not the flattened list. Test: `DONE: …/LinearViewer/pull/2360 and …/simple-dispatcher/pull/330` → `sessionPrs(...).reported[0] === …/LinearViewer/pull/2360`.
- **inside** (live: the leftover prompt, the held wake and the runner's `[done]` url name the build's own PR). *After the deploy* of both PRs, on the first eligible autopilot `implementation` that reads a sibling PR, check that `GET /dispatch/{leftoverId}/prompt`, the parent wake and the runner's `[done]` url all name the PR that build opened. Older runners still fill `url` by mention count, so Harbour's `DONE:`-first read is what protects them. **Monitor:** server log. `[leftover] hold … claim-lost` appears only beside a `[leftover] queued` for the same item, never alone.
- **inside** (claim with no row if the server dies mid-request). LIN-4347's re-review accepted this as a recorded residual (`runs-and-dispatch` Waiting). Unchanged.
- **Rollback:** each PR is a single squash merge and can be reverted. `leftoverClaimedAt` is additive and nothing else reads it.

### Verdict
Request Changes

The PR-selection fix is correct and well tested in both repositories, and it meets every acceptance sentence. The `claimLeftoverFor` addition in #2360 brings in a stall that `main` does not have: a LIN-3805 re-report after a skip plus a transient wake withdrawal is held forever. **Next action: `implementation` on this task.** Release the claim on every post-claim skip, add the repro test, and fix the `sessionPrs` grouping on #330 in the same pass. Then re-run review.

**Revision for the review (`8c9ec493`): both findings fixed, CI green on both PRs.**

- https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2360 at head `57f70faa`. CI green: Unit tests, E2E 1–4/4, Secret scan, CI success. 24309/24309 unit tests pass locally.
- https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/330 at head `104daf7`. CI `unit tests` green. Full suite 4270 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped.

Finding by finding:

1. **A claim winner that skips strands the parent wake on a re-report (defect, #2360).** Fixed as prescribed. Every post-claim skip (`no-base-url`, `no-workspace`, `enqueue-<status>`) now calls the new `DispatchQueueStore.releaseLeftoverClaim(urlKey, itemId)` first. The release is best-effort and logs `[leftover] claim-release-failed` on a fault. One departure: it does `$set: {leftoverClaimedAt: null}` rather than `$unset`. No store in `lib/` uses `$unset` and the test mock lacks it, and the claim filter already reads null as unclaimed.
   - The review's repro is a test in `tests/unit/lin-4375-session-pr-wins.test.js`: enqueue 503 `OWNER_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE` plus `grant-mint-transient:x`, then a healthy re-report. That re-report queues exactly one leftover row; when it skips too, it wakes the parent exactly once, and a third report adds none.
   - On `a874f03f` both versions failed with `claim-lost` and `actual: 0, expected: 1`. A mutation (only the enqueue path back to plain `skip`) failed both again.
   - The concurrent exactly-one-row test still passes.
   - The hook header, `dispatch-and-proxy.md` "One claim per row" and the `runs-and-dispatch` lesson and Waiting entry are updated.
2. **Two PRs on one `DONE:` line: the runner and Harbour disagreed (#330).** Fixed. `sessionPrs` now reverses groups per `DONE:` line, so `DONE: …/LinearViewer/pull/2360 and …/simple-dispatcher/pull/330` puts LinearViewer first. There is a pure test and a `buildEvidence` test; both failed on the old code with `actual …/simple-dispatcher/pull/330`.
   - The Harbour side already took the first PR on a line. But within one message it took the oldest report line, while the runner takes the newest, so `reportedPrUrlOf` now takes the newest line. A test for this failed on the old code with `actual …/2357`.

**Residuals, recorded in the hook header and the architecture doc:**
- The accepted "server dies mid-request" claim, now joined by "a release write fails". Both are in the Waiting entry.
- A second `[done]` that lands between a skipping winner's release and the mint of its wake can queue a leftover row beside that wake. This is main's pre-claim behaviour, but only in that window.

Next: re-run review. Merge and deploy are not mine. After deploy, the live check from the review still applies: the leftover prompt, the parent wake and the runner's `[done]` url should all name the build's own PR, and `claim-lost` should never appear in the log without a matching `queued`.

### Leftovers

PRs:
- https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2360, head `298bad5b`, CI green.
- https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/330, head `41e1cec8`, CI green.

- **Tidied:** the header of `tests/unit/lin-4375-session-pr-wins.test.js` listed only the PR choice and the concurrent claim. It now also names the claim release and the PR order (newest line, first PR on it).
- **Tidied:** the "Which PR" bullet in `dispatch-and-proxy.md` now states the order among report lines, the same order as the runner's `sessionPrs`.
- **Tidied (lesson):** simple-dispatcher's `stop-hook-and-relay` note has a new lesson. Within `DONE:` lines, the newest line comes first and its PRs keep their order, matching Harbour's `reportedPrUrlOf`.
- **Noted (in the revision commit):** in `runs-and-dispatch`, a lesson on giving the claim back on every skip. The claim-with-no-row Waiting entry now also covers a failed release write. No waiting entry was settled by this change.
- **For close-out:** nothing.

The PR-order rule lives in both repos, `sessionPrs` and `reportedPrUrlOf`. That is the runner/Harbour boundary, not a copy to remove: each comment and each repo's notes point at the other. The existing Waiting entries about the `DONE:` sentinel being spelled twice still stand, unchanged.

## Review — LIN-4375 (re-review of the revision)

I reviewed Harbour [PR #2360](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2360) at head `298bad5b` and simple-dispatcher [PR #330](https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/330) at head `41e1cec8`. Both are open and mergeable. Both are based on current `main`: LinearViewer `d5d18e6d`, simple-dispatcher `4aee0c9`.

CI: green on both heads. #2360: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4/4, Secret scan (source), CI success. #330: unit tests. I also ran both ticket test files at the heads: Harbour 15/15 and runner 9/9.

### The two findings from the last review (`8c9ec493`)
1. **A claim winner that skips strands the parent wake. Fixed.** `lib/dispatch-leftover-hook.js` now routes every skip after the claim (`no-base-url`, `no-workspace`, `enqueue-<status>`) through `skipClaimed`, which calls `releaseLeftoverClaim` first. Skips before the claim (decision skips) and the `claim-lost` hold correctly do not release.
   - The release sets the field to `null` instead of using `$unset`. That is equivalent, because the claim filter `leftoverClaimedAt: null` also matches an absent field.
   - The release is best-effort and logs `[leftover] claim-release-failed`. The repro test from the last review is now in the suite.
2. **Two PRs on one `DONE:` line. Fixed in both repos.** The runner now reverses groups, not the flattened list (`newestGroupsFirst`). Harbour's `reportedPrUrlOf` now reads the newest report line first, then the first PR on that line. The two now agree.

### Mutation checks (each reverted; worktrees removed)
- Harbour: release made a no-op → 2 fail (both re-report tests). Only the enqueue path set back to a plain `skip` → the same 2 fail. `reportedPrUrlOf` set to read the oldest line first → 1 fails ("newest line wins"). Reported-PR loop removed from `prUrlOfFeedback` → 6 fail, including the store-level prompt and held-wake test. Claim check bypassed → 1 fails ("exactly one leftover row").
- simple-dispatcher: `groups.flat().reverse()` → 2 fail. `selectCanonical` made to ignore the session's own PRs → 4 fail. `buildEvidence` unwired back to `tracked[0]` → 4 fail. `gh pr create` harvesting removed → 2 fail.

Every load-bearing test fails when the code path it claims is removed.

### Other checks
- **Scope and staleness.** Since the last review, the changes are exactly the two fixes, plus doc, lesson and test-header tidies. No anchored file changed on `main` after `d5d18e6d`. The `claimLeftoverFor` overrun was already noted and accepted.
- **Regression.** The recent history of `dispatch-leftover-hook.js`, `dispatch-wake.js`, `hook.js` and `links.js` has no reverts and no earlier fix that this undoes.
- **Callers.** All `prUrlOfFeedback` callers inherit the fix: `dispatch-leftover.js:76` (leftover prompt) and `dispatch-store.js:3415/3422/3521` (held-wake notes). Nothing else reads `leftoverClaimedAt`.
- **Format.** The runner's `[done]` message is `[done] Task completed in …`, with no URL. Its evidence entries start `[evidence]`. So Harbour's `[done]`-line match cannot pick up the runner's frequency choice from message text. Relayed assistant text is posted raw, so `^\s*DONE:` matches it.
- **Class.** The class is still "which PR is this session's", and both of its places are handled. `run-evidence.js` and `ci-wake-sweep.js` collect all PRs on purpose, so they are a different mechanism. There are no unhandled siblings inside the class.
- **Leftovers** (`93a18ac0`): the tidies are present in both diffs. The two "`DONE:` spelled twice" Waiting entries are worded to land. Close-out has nothing to fix.

### Against the As-asked block
- "When a session reports a PR on its `DONE:` line, or opened a PR in its own transcript, that PR is the `[done]` entry's `url`…": **met** (`selectCanonical`/`sessionPrs`, mutation-checked).
- "`prUrlOfFeedback` returns the PR the session reported … ahead of an `url` field that disagrees": **met** (`reportedPrUrlOf`, mutation-checked).
- "Each repo has a test … mentions another PR more often … the session's own PR wins": **met** in both repos (#2357 ×26 vs #2359).
- Problem, witness, why, anchors and priority are context. The fix goes to their cause in both repos.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **inside** (the PR-selection class; the live path end to end). *After the deploy* of both PRs: on the first eligible autopilot `implementation` that reads a sibling PR, check that `GET /dispatch/{leftoverId}/prompt`, the parent wake and the runner's `[done]` url all name the PR the build opened. CI drives each side against fixtures, never a real runner posting to a real Harbour.
- **inside** (the claim this PR adds, against real Mongo or MangoDB). The claim and release tests run on the test mock. The claim relies on `{leftoverClaimedAt: null}` matching both an absent field and a released null. **Monitor:** server log. `[leftover] hold … claim-lost` should only appear beside a `[leftover] queued` for the same item, never alone. It is only proven in production because no CI test runs against the real store.
- **inside** (recorded residuals, accepted). A claim with no row remains possible if the server dies mid-request or a release write fails; the monitor signal is `[leftover] claim-release-failed`. A re-report between a release and the wake mint can queue a leftover row beside the wake. Both are in the `runs-and-dispatch` Waiting entries and the hook header, and are unchanged by this review.
- **Rollback:** revert each PR's squash-merge commit. `leftoverClaimedAt` is additive and nothing else reads it. Older runners stay protected by Harbour's `DONE:`-first read, so the two PRs can be deployed in either order.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

Both findings from the last review are fixed and mutation-checked. Every acceptance sentence is met, and CI is green on `298bad5b` and `41e1cec8`. Close-out has nothing to fix. It should merge both PRs, then run the post-deploy live check and watch the `claim-lost` monitor.

## Close-out — LIN-4375

**Merged and deployed.**
- Harbour [#2360](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2360): squash `459f8711`, merged at reviewed head `298bad5b` with `--match-head-commit`. The Railway production deploy of `459f8711` succeeded at 06:45Z, and the live footer shows `459f8711`.
- simple-dispatcher [#330](https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/330): squash `cb79e00`, merged at reviewed head `41e1cec8` with `--match-head-commit`. The host's runner checkout is at `cb79e00`, and `watch-restart.sh` restarted the dispatcher at 06:33:25Z.

**How it meets what was asked.** Re-review `964c9238` covers this. All three acceptance sentences are met and mutation-checked: `selectCanonical`/`sessionPrs` in the runner, `reportedPrUrlOf` in `prUrlOfFeedback`, and one test per repo with #2357 ×26 vs #2359.

**Changes made in close-out:** none. Re-review said close-out had nothing to fix, and both PRs were still based on current `main` at merge (LinearViewer `d5d18e6d`, simple-dispatcher `4aee0c9`). The re-review also asked for no note entries.

**Final CI**, on the merged heads:
- #2360 (`298bad5b`): Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4/4, Secret scan (source) and CI success, all green.
- #330 (`41e1cec8`): unit tests green.

**Ledger** (re-review `964c9238`, "What CI Did Not Prove"):
1. **inside: the live PR-selection path end to end.** Partly settled.
   - *Run on the landed code against the real witness*, LIN-4374's build (#2357 mentioned 26 times, #2359 on `DONE:`). This is the exact distinguishing precondition.
     - Harbour `prUrlOfFeedback` at `459f8711`, on build `ae1954d9`'s real feedback, returns **#2359**. That holds both at the first `[done]` and over the full lineage, even though the runner's `url` field says #2357. At base `d5d18e6d` it returns #2357.
     - Runner `buildEvidence` at `cb79e00`, on that build's real transcript, returns `[done]` url **#2359**, with the evidence entries still in frequency order. At base `4aee0c9` it returns #2357.
   - **Not run: a real runner posting to the real Harbour.** The check: on an autopilot `implementation` that reads a sibling PR, `GET /dispatch/{leftoverId}/prompt`, the parent wake and the `[done]` url all name the PR that build opened. *Why not run:* no such build has finished since the deploy (LIN-4376 is at plan). *Who can run it:* the operator, or the close-out of the next eligible autopilot build. This is recorded on both PRs.
2. **inside: the claim against real Mongo.** Settled by the monitor review named: the Harbour server log. `[leftover] hold … claim-lost` must only appear beside a `[leftover] queued` for the same item, never alone, and `[leftover] claim-release-failed` signals a stranded claim. I read the deployed container's log through `railway logs` at close-out: it has no `[leftover]` lines yet, because no `[done]` has arrived since the restart.
3. **inside: recorded residuals.** Already accepted by review. They stay recorded in the `runs-and-dispatch` Waiting entries and the hook header, unchanged.
- **Rollback:** as review named, revert each PR's squash commit (`459f8711`, `cb79e00`). `leftoverClaimedAt` is additive, and the two repos can be reverted in either order.

**Related tickets.**
- LIN-4347 (this blocks it) stays open. Its remaining steps (live observations, John's outstanding ruling, parent re-review) are its own. Its close-out items 1–2 are now done; I've noted that on it.
- LIN-4374 is already Done.

**Follow-ups filed:** none. The ledger has no outside items.

**Description:** archived to the snapshots, then a short stub written below the `## As asked` block (nothing had been written there before).

relatedIssue.title: After the merge: read it blind, ask the builder, tidy what it left
Review reads the leftovers, close-out writes the notes (3/3), and the post-deploy demonstration
